children: The New York Yankees are close to completing a transaction that would give Apollo Global Management
a 16% economic stake in the franchise and value the team at more than $12 billion, according to New York Post reporter Charles Gasparino.
The Steinbrenner family would remain firmly in control with ownership of slightly more than 60%. Its stake would be diluted by no more than 3%, while Apollo
would become the team’s second-largest investor.

Under the reported structure, Apollo would initially acquire an 8% stake and receive preferred shares that could convert into an additional 8% after four years. Major League Baseball limits private equity firms to 15% ownership of a team, though the league is expected to grant an exception.

The $2.6 billion investment combines debt and equity financing. Some of the money would refinance debt at lower rates, while also giving the Yankees more resources for player spending and protection against a possible labor stoppage. Apollo
executive Al Tylis is expected to join the 13-member board of Yankees Global Enterprises.

For investors, the transaction highlights the rapid institutionalization of professional sports. Scarce franchises, lucrative media rights and relatively resilient fan demand have attracted private equity firms seeking assets that may appreciate independently of public markets. The deal also could establish a new valuation benchmark for baseball teams and other premium sports properties.
The investment is said to include Yankees Global Enterprises, which has interests in the YES Network, Legends Hospitality and Italian soccer club AC Milan. Apollo’s
immediate investment closed in August, while the purchase of interests from existing limited partners is in its final stages.

Some longtime Yankees investors sought liquidity for estate-planning purposes. Apollo, meanwhile, needed a major investment for its new $6 billion sports fund. The firm’s other sports holdings include a majority interest in Atlético Madrid and a stake in the company behind professional pickleball.
If completed, the transaction would rank among the largest private equity investments in a sports franchise and could position the Yankees as baseball’s most valuable team, the N.Y. Post reported.

title: N.Y. Yankees near deal giving Apollo 16% stake in storied franchise
